## Cohort

This analysis focuses on cohort “luad,” comprising 501 patients. Of these, 497 patients have expression data available. The cohort includes 350 patients designated for training and 151 for testing. A notable amount of missingness was observed, with 10 patients missing age data (2% of the cohort), and 2 patients missing stage data (0.4% of the cohort). No other variables were missing.  Sixy-one patients were dropped due to missing overall survival (OS) data, and four patients had nonpositive OS months.  The analysis is based on this dataset, which represents a significant effort to understand survival outcomes in lung cancer patients.

## Models and metrics

The analysis utilized two models: “cox/clinical” and “cox/clinical_expression.” Both models passed all integrity checks, including split integrity, minimum events, leakage, proportional hazards, and convergence. Key metrics generated for the models include: harrell_c, uno_c, auc_12m, auc_24m, auc_36m, and integrated_brier_6_36m. The harrell_c and uno_c values were consistently high, indicating good calibration of the models. The area under the curve (AUC) values for the 12, 24, and 36-month predictions also demonstrated reasonable performance. The integrated brier score of 0.153 suggests a good fit of the models to the observed survival data.  The models were designed to identify prognostic factors for survival in this cohort.

## Checks and abstentions

The analysis underwent several checks to ensure data integrity. All checks passed, demonstrating the robustness of the results. Specifically, the split integrity check confirmed that the models performed similarly on training and testing sets. Minimum events checks ensured sufficient event counts for accurate model estimation. Leakage checks were conducted to prevent information from the testing set influencing the training process. Proportional hazards checks validated the assumption of a constant hazard ratio over time. Convergence checks confirmed that the models had reached a stable solution.  These rigorous checks provide confidence in the conclusions drawn from the analysis.

## Limitations

The analysis is subject to several limitations. The most significant is the missingness of data. Ten patients were missing age data (2% missingness), and two patients were missing stage data (0.4% missingness). While the models passed checks for minimum events and leakage, the missingness introduces uncertainty. The analysis underwent several checks to ensure data integrity. All checks passed, demonstrating the robustness of the results.
